summary: The docstring guarantees that non-__ANDROID__ frames are treated as live, 'which is the conservative direction: it can report a line some other guard excludes, never hide one'. The first half is implemented (:96, live = True for an unknown condition); the second is not. The #else handler at :104-106 inverts live unconditionally, including for a frame whose condition was unknown-and-assumed-live, so the #else arm of any conditional the script does not understand is marked dead and never scanned. The guarantee is inverted exactly where it is claimed. This file was added at e81aaca8ae, after 174f50669e wrote the pass-1 audit, so no audit has read it.
scenario: A lane adds a desktop-only token inside the #else of a `#if defined(__APPLE__)`, a `#if DEBUG_NV2A_GL`, or a `#ifdef GL_FOO` suffix-fallback chain -- which is the idiomatic place to put a portability fallback, and gl/constants.h:37-69 shows the codebase already does this -- runs gles_token_check.py on a machine with no NDK, reads '0 findings', and pushes. The arm64-v8a job fails, which is H1 again with the check that exists to prevent it reporting clean, and the script's own closing advice never prints because there is no finding. The docstring compounds it: a reader who has read 'never hide one' will not re-derive the coverage, and this repository has already paid twice for a comment that was believed (vk/draw.c L2, quoted in this PR's own diff).
remediation: Record on each frame whether __ANDROID__ decided it, and invert on #else only for those frames; leave an unknown frame live in both arms. `stack.append({'live': live, 'known': known, 'tested': tested})` and, in the #else handler, `if stack[-1]['known']: stack[-1]['live'] = not stack[-1]['live']` -- otherwise fall through leaving it live. #elif wants the same treatment: it already forces live = True, which is right, but it must also stop a following #else from inverting a value that was never derived. Then ADD THE MUTANT BELOW AS A FIXTURE AND CONFIRM IT TRIPS -- a check whose new invariant has no failing case is a check that has not been tested -- and confirm the fixed script still gives 0 findings over hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl, which is the regression guard on the fix. MEDIUM and not HIGH: the failure is a false clean in a pre-push convenience check, the Android CI job is the gate of record and is green on every PR, the script is not wired into preflight.sh, and no emulator behaviour is affected.
evidence: MUTANT, four lines, using a token from the script's own DESKTOP_ONLY list: `#if defined(SOME_OTHER_THING)` / `static int a(void) { return 0; }` / `#else` / `static GLenum b(void) { return GL_SRC1_ALPHA; }` / `#endif` -> '1 file scanned, 0 findings', exit 0. The same token at the same place without the conditional is caught. NOT HYPOTHETICAL ON THIS TREE: instrumenting the script's own frame stack over its default target hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl, 114 non-blank lines in 21 frames sit inside an #else arm marked dead on an unknown condition. Two are ordinary code an Android build compiles -- gl/debug.c:66, `#if defined(__APPLE__) ... #else glEnable(GL_DEBUG_OUTPUT); ... #endif`, where __APPLE__ is undefined on Android so the #else arm is exactly what arm64-v8a compiles; and gl/debug.h:53, `#if DEBUG_NV2A_GL ... #else ... #endif`, whose #else arm is the macro set every non-debug build uses. The other 19 are #ifdef __aarch64__ scalar fallbacks in surface.c/texture.c and the #else tails of the constants.h suffix chains. Nothing in the hidden region trips the curated list today, so the current '0 findings' is a true result -- true by luck, not by the check. The script is otherwise good and its power test is real: run against gl/draw.c at 7ffcd2bc it reports :151 GL_SRC1_ALPHA and :153 GL_ONE_MINUS_SRC1_ALPHA, the same two lines by number the arm64-v8a compiler reported. I re-ran that on the output words, not the exit code.

summary: The comment at :102-104 states the requirement -- 'a request for OPENGL on a host with no usable GL context silently continues on Vulkan, and a run mislabelled that way is worse than no run' -- and the code at :105-107 enforces only that SOME renderer was reported. $got is never compared to $RENDERER. A run that requested OPENGL and came up on Vulkan prints one informational line and exits 0, with captures extracted under the OPENGL tag. This file was added at 645462d08d, after the pass-1 audit commit, so no audit has read it.
scenario: A sweep loops the runner over OPENGL and VULKAN on a host whose GL context is unavailable -- a headless container whose xvfb server came up without GLX, a driver change, a build configured without CONFIG_OPENGL. Both arms come up on Vulkan, both exit 0, both produce 236 captures, and the OPENGL arm's captures are Vulkan's. Nothing fails, so the mismatch survives only as one line of stdout in a log nobody re-reads, and the conclusion that reads out of that data is 'GL is now byte-identical to Vulkan' -- which is, to within a few captures, the headline this PR publishes. The instrument's silent-failure mode and the lane's result have the same shape, so the instrument has to be the thing that refuses.
remediation: Make it a die, beside the one already there: case "$(printf '%s' "$got" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" in "$(printf '%s' "$RENDERER" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')") ;; *) die "requested $RENDERER but the run came up on $got -- see $LOG" ;; esac. Confirm it trips by running once with RENDERER=OPENGL against a fixture log whose renderer line says Vulkan, and assert on the message rather than the exit code: the script exits non-zero for a dozen other reasons.
evidence: Everything the comparison needs is already in hand. pgraph.c:1190 prints 'nv2a: renderer: %s' from renderers[g_config.display.renderer]->name AFTER the fallback chooser at :1141-1153, so it is the selected renderer and not the requested one -- which is what makes the script's chosen signal the right one. The two values are gl/renderer.c:344 .name = "OpenGL" and vk/renderer.c:2602 .name = "Vulkan", against the script's OPENGL / VULKAN, so a case-insensitive compare is one line. THIS PUTS NO PUBLISHED NUMBER IN DOUBT and I do not claim it does: the runs behind the result table reported differing per-capture values between the two backends, which a both-on-Vulkan pair cannot produce. The defect is in what the committed instrument will permit next time on a machine that is not this one, which is the reason the PR itself gives for committing it.

summary: The PR body's L1 disposition says 'the call site now expresses the GLES exclusion the way the other two sites do'. It expresses it the way gl/renderer.c does -- #ifndef __ANDROID__ -- and not the way psh.c:2018 and :3568 do, which is the run-time term `&& !ps->opts.gles`. The asymmetry pass 1 named is reduced from three-ways-two to three-ways-two with the membership changed, not removed.
scenario: Pass 1's L1 scenario is untouched: on a GLES-capable build that is not Android, gl/renderer.c's setter runs, the psh.c gates suppress the index-1 output, and gl/draw.c still names a SRC1 factor against a shader that has none -- undefined rather than an error, so it arrives as corrupted colour and not as a diagnostic. It stays LOW for the reason pass 1 gave: no such build exists, and gl/shaders.c:357/360 ties gles to __ANDROID__. The finding is only that the PR body claims a convergence the code does not make, and the code comment at :445-458 is honest about the choice while the body is not.
remediation: One clause in the PR body: the call site now excludes GLES the way gl/renderer.c does, by preprocessor, because the tokens are absent rather than merely unwanted, while psh.c keeps the run-time term because a shader gate has no token to be absent. The prose fix is enough.
